text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad defended the role of state investment fund Khazanah Nasional in an abortive deal to acquire Hong Kong-based power firm CEPA.

-- A parcel bomb which exploded outside a courier depot in New Zealand on Wednesday and injuring two Malaysians, went through customs and security inspections undetected at five airports in two continents, sources said.
-- The Employees' Provident Fund has issued a list of 25 fund managers which have been allowed to make investments for EPF members who wish to invest part of their savings in the capital market.
-- Malayan Banking Bhd is eyeing a controlling stake in a Philippine commercial bank, Philippines National-Republic Bank.
-- DCB Holdings Bhd said it has received permission from the central bank to begin negotiations with Rashid Hussain Bhd to a restructuring scheme involving itself and Kwong Yik Bank Bhd.
